display.purpose: The home h1; page-header h1s sit at 3rem to 3.75rem.

headline.purpose: Section h2s in blackletter, 2.25rem rising to 3rem.

numeral.purpose: Every numeral in a medallion and on the dial.

title.purpose: h3 and h4, row names, definition terms, in the text face.

figures.purpose: Sums, reduction chains, dates and scores in tabular lining figures.

label.purpose: Small-caps meta, captions and list terms (font-variant-caps: all-small-caps). Never above a heading.

shadows.name: cell-rule
shadows.purpose: Draws the shared iron rules between cells of a ruled grid. A line, not a shadow; the system has no elevation shadows.

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: The one easing curve: the dial settling and the hand swinging.

motion.name: dial-settle
motion.value: 1.6s var(--ease-settle) backwards, 90ms stagger per ring, outer first
motion.purpose: On load each body leaves twelve o'clock and settles on its numeral. Off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: dial-turn
motion.purpose: Hand and bodies turning to a pressed row or a new reading. Off under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: numeral-light
motion.purpose: A rim numeral changing between iron and gilt.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour, border and background changes on hover, focus and press.

narrative.overview:
Numen is drawn as a gothic astronomical clock read at night. A name and a birth date turn its rings; a hand points at the number being read; the sums that produced each number are written out beside it. The ground is night, the one coloured field is an ultramarine sky, a thin vermilion band of twilight crosses the dial, and everything that is drawn rather than read is a gilt line. The system is flat and ruled: nothing floats, nothing glows, nothing sits in a box.

Density is that of a reference plate, not a landing page. Text is set at a generous reading size in a pen-cut text face, figures line up in columns, and blackletter is saved for the few things that deserve to be carved: the wordmark, the two top heading levels and the numerals. The instrument does the persuading, so the page around it stays quiet.

The system rejects the category's starfield-and-glow hero and the centred headline over a card form. It also rejects card chrome of any kind: content sits between rules.
keyCharacteristics: Night ground, one ultramarine sky field, gilt lines, bone lettering.
Two shapes only: the circle (dial, medallion) and the rule (plates, grids).
Blackletter for h1, h2, the wordmark and numerals; a text face for everything read.
Vermilion is rationed; gilt is structural; unlit things are drawn in iron, not hidden.
Every sum is shown in tabular figures next to the number it produced.
One authored motion: the dial settling.

rules.name: The Rubric Rule
rules.body: Among numbers and tags, vermilion marks a master number or a karmic debt and nothing else. Its two other standing places are fixed: the twilight band on the dial, and a field in error. It is never decoration, emphasis or a call to action.

rules.name: The Gilt Is Drawn Rule
rules.body: Gilt belongs to what is drawn or pressed: rings, rules, numerals and figures, links, field labels, and the one primary button. It is never used to emphasise a word inside a heading; an `em` in a heading stays upright and in the heading's own bone.

rules.name: The Iron Rule
rules.body: A position that is not lit is still drawn. Numerals no ring points at stay on the rim in iron; inactive rings stay at 38% gilt. Nothing is hidden to show that it is off.

rules.name: The Carved Letters Rule
rules.body: Blackletter is for h1, h2, the wordmark and numerals. h3 and below, labels, buttons, nav and every sentence are Texturina: below the top two levels blackletter is too dense to scan.

rules.name: The No Label Above A Heading Rule
rules.body: A heading opens its own section. A small-caps label may sit beside a heading as meta, or under a medallion as its caption, or as a term in a list; it never sits on the line above a heading to introduce it.

rules.name: The Shown Sum Rule
rules.body: A number never appears without a route to its working. Sums are set in tabular lining figures in pale gilt, one sum to a line, with `→` between reductions.

rules.name: The Three Grounds Rule
rules.body: A surface is night, a well, or sky. Lift is never shown; a thing is separated from its neighbour by a rule or by changing ground.

dos: Do put every number in a round medallion with a blackletter numeral, and use the master and karmic variants whenever the number is one.
Do separate things with rules: gilt double rule to open, hairline to close, iron between cells.
Do keep unlit positions on the page in iron (`bone-600` numerals, `iron` rules, rings at 38%).
Do show the working next to the number, in tabular lining figures, one sum to a line.
Do keep the six rings in one order everywhere: Life Path, Expression, Soul Urge, Personality, Birthday, Maturity.
Do give every focusable thing the 2px `gold-200` outline offset 3px, and keep touch targets at 2.75rem.
Do keep the privacy promise visible beside any field that takes a name or a birth date.
Do turn the dial off under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` and gate any new movement the same way.
donts: Don't use vermilion for anything but master numbers, karmic debts, the dial's twilight band and a field in error.
Don't colour a word in a heading gilt, or italicise it; heading emphasis stays in the heading's ink.
Don't set blackletter below h2, in buttons, labels, nav or running text.
Don't place a small-caps label on the line above a heading.
Don't draw a card: no rounded box, no four-sided border around a block of content, no shadow, no fill other than the sky field.
Don't add shadows, glows, blur, gradients or starfields.
Don't round a corner. A thing is square or it is a circle.
Don't add a second authored animation. State changes are 150ms to 200ms colour transitions; the dial settling is the only choreography.
Don't style an advertisement to resemble a plate of content, or place one where it interrupts the dial.
